readme: CANONICAL store registry (2026-07-26, estate-audit item #5). One row per store the board tracks. Scripts that need the full store list read THIS file (sorted by 'order'); audit-store-registry.ps1 scans live scripts daily and flags any hardcoded list that names >=3 stores but not all of them (the publish-store-guide/publish-deals-page Fareway-drift class). Add a new store HERE FIRST, then run audit-store-registry.ps1 to find every site the change must reach. 'allowed_subsets' documents lines that legitimately name only some stores; check 6 of that audit re-resolves every entry (the file must exist and its 'contains' needle must still be present in it), because an exemption is a standing decision and a standing decision nobody re-checks rots - four of the thirty entries had already gone dead when that check was added on 2026-09-05, two of them naming scripts retired on 2026-08-22. 'walled': true marks the four stores whose prices can only be captured through a human browser session behind a bot wall (Walmart, Sam's Club, Aldi, Fareway) - build-rescue-worklist.ps1 reads THIS FLAG to decide which stores get a rescue term list. It is an explicit flag and not a match on 'capture' on purpose: Aldi's capture string starts with 'server (Flipp flyerkit JSON)' because its AD is a server pull, while its shelf prices come off the Instacart storefront by hand, so any substring test for 'browser' silently drops it.

The region under test, audit-food-category.ps1, never branches on store - it uses the store field only for the food-class-allowlist key (line 91) and the report text (lines 93 and 120) and decides the class on commodity id plus item name against the category-exclude library - so 3 stores prove the contract for all 7 and four more rows would add zero coverage while making the fixture read as a roster it is not. The fixture is frozen under the guard-fixture rule and must never be regenerated from the board. The needle is taken from INSIDE the string literal rather than from the assignment prefix, so it matches both the widened AST statement text and the raw line; if the fixture text is ever rewritten the needle stops matching and the guard speaks up again, which is the correct behaviour. The region under test decides class membership on the item NAME alone (audit-food-category.ps1:88, `$nm -imatch $pat`); $s.store is used at line 91 only to key the known-wrong allowlist, which can only SILENCE a finding, and at 93/120 only to print it - so no store absent from this fixture could turn its expected exit 0 into a failure, and the four named prove the contract for all seven. The fixture is frozen under the guard-fixture rule and test-auditors.ps1:995 says so four lines above it: NEVER REGENERATE THESE ROWS FROM THE BOARD. Registered rather than edited, which is the whole point. The needle is taken from INSIDE the string literal, not from the assignment prefix, so it matches both the widened AST statement text and the raw line; if the fixture is ever rewritten the needle stops matching, the guard speaks up again, and the orphaned-exemption check (check 6) reports this entry as dead - which is the correct behaviour in both directions. promoted_prefixes_readme: out\regular files whose prefix is NOT a store's regular_prefix because they are not a store PULL. They are one-shot promoted captures written by another lane, and check 3 of audit-store-registry.ps1 accepts them. Registered rather than deleted (2026-08-30, queue 2026-08-22-2c3e88): input-usage.json shows hunter-walmart-regular-2026-08-16.json first_used 08-21, last_used the 2026-08-26 build, uses=5, so deleting them would silently drop adjudicated cells from live builds. NOTE what registering here does NOT do: guard 6 in guards.ps1 enumerates prefixes from the FILES it finds, not from this registry, so its 'could NOT evaluate' warn for these seven stands - correctly. Each prefix holds exactly one capture, so there genuinely is no history to compare a thin file against, and silencing that warn from here would be dressing up an unwatched store as a watched one.

pull_profile_readme: Per-store pull mechanics, read by that store's agent module so pacing is versioned data instead of a number retyped into a console snippet. RULES: (1) every value is MEASURED or marked proposed/unmeasured - never guess a safe rate, an unpaced Sams sweep walled at 207 of 595 terms on 2026-08-15; (2) this block records HOW to pull, never WHAT a store carries. Do not add learned empty/absent terms here. A term recorded as empty during a wall would silently stop being checked forever, which is the contested-flag-baselined-away class: unchecked is never not-carried.
